title: The Greatest Shortcut for Leaders Is Reading Books
author: Ryan Holiday
summary: Ryan Holiday argues that reading is the shortcut every leader must take, allowing access to five thousand years of human wisdom on problems never before encountered. Leaders from Truman to Mattis recognized that learning from history and others' experience prevents painful trial and error. Intentional reading of books that develop empathy and wisdom compounds into transformed leadership and personal growth far more efficiently than learning solely from experience. Books provide meditative, spiritual benefits beyond content alone; imagining scenes builds empathy and changes how readers perceive the world and their role in it. Leaders who spend time with books gain meditative focus, empathy development, and access to proven wisdom across centuries of human problem-solving.
points: Leaders face problems they have never experienced, but humans have written about nearly every challenge for five thousand years through accessible books.
Reading is a shortcut that compresses the trial and error of a lifetime into accelerated learning; ignoring books means learning slowly and painfully through experience.
Books provide meditative, spiritual benefits beyond content: imagining scenes builds empathy and changes how readers perceive the world and their role in it.
Great leaders were avid readers who applied historical lessons to their contexts: Marcus Aurelius with philosophy, Malcolm X with diverse texts, Oprah with transformative ideas.
Intentional reading selection matters; asking people you admire what changed their lives reveals books worth the focus of your finite time and energy.
quotes: Not every reader is a leader, but every leader is a reader. You have to be.
How can we possibly justify learning slowly, by experience or trial and error, what we can easily pick up in a book?
Being busy at work or at home isn't a good reason not to read. It's an argument for why you should.
The Roman Emperor Marcus Aurelius prized the ability to read attentively, mostly philosophy texts, and used what he learned to reign masterfully over his domain.

No one gets anywhere in this world in any really and endurable manner without some recourse to books. Reading is also a shortcut, a way to get where you want to get without having to learn by painful trial and error.” Archived from Daily Stoic on April 20, 2026 by Tim.
